tool_schemas.name: get_service_status
tool_schemas.description: Current version per region, health and error rate of a service.

tool_schemas.name: list_deployments
tool_schemas.description: Release history for a service with health status (oldest first).

tool_schemas.name: rollback
tool_schemas.description: Roll a service back to a previously released version in all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: deploy
tool_schemas.description: Deploy a version of a service to all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: create_incident
tool_schemas.description: Open an incident; this pages the on-call engineer.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy - rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 production deploy (error rate was 0.18 across us-east, us-west, and eu-west). Per the runbook, I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent production release that was healthy, in all three production regions. Post-rollback status: all regions on v2.3.0, healthy=true, error rate 0.002. v2.3.1 is marked unhealthy in production and was not redeployed. Follow-up: investigate the v2.3.1 failure before any re-release. Note that v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). It is now healthy, with an error rate of 0.002, down from 0.18 on v2.3.1.

v2.3.0 was the most recent production release marked healthy. v2.3.1 is marked unhealthy, so the rollback did not need change-manager approval.

I opened SEV2 incident INC-0001 for checkout-api, which paged the on-call engineer. The summary covers the v2.3.1 failure, the rollback, and the post-rollback status. The first attempt to create the incident timed out, so I retried with the same idempotency key. The incident was created once.

Open follow-up: v2.3.1 needs investigation before it is re-released. v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging.

content.text: The most recent production release that was healthy is v2.3.0. v2.3.1 is the unhealthy release now serving all three regions. I'll roll back to v2.3.0. It has a healthy production history, so the change-manager approval requirement doesn't apply.
